messages:
ops-bot: [ALERT] 02:14 UTC - hosted-api/gpu-pool-us-west-2 is at 100% GPU utilization and request_queue_length > 12k for 4m. Autoscaler attempted 3 scale actions; last failed due to operator timeout. Investigate and acknowledge if oncall.

emma: acked. I'm oncall. seeing p95 generation latency -> 3.8s, p99 -> 18s, 503 spikes starting at 02:10 UTC. Dashboard: https://console.redwood.ai/metrics/r/hosted/queue

siva: tagging @emma — looks like allocator operator pod restarted at 02:09:52 with OOM, then backoff. kube events show 'scale action timed out waiting for nodepool quota'.

emma: copy. listing recent autoscaler attempts:
```
# last 3 attempts
2026-03-14T02:09:58Z ACTION scale_up target=4->6 reason=gpu_pool_saturation
2026-03-14T02:10:22Z STATUS error operator_timeout
2026-03-14T02:11:05Z ACTION scale_up target=4->6 reason=gpu_pool_saturation
2026-03-14T02:11:45Z STATUS error quota_exceeded (provider)
```

nanya: customer-impact note: we're seeing retries/timeouts for some streaming sessions. CS alerted a handful of accounts on higher tiers — they reported user-facing slowdowns and intermittent failures.

mike: any mitigation we can do that doesn't require cloud quota? can we shift traffic to smaller quantized model or spill to secondary region?

emma: yes. immediate mitigation plan: 1) enable conservative global throttling at 85% of capacity to stop unbounded queue growth, 2) enable model_fallback policy that routes new requests to quantized-medium variants (lower GPU mem), 3) open temporary routing to eu-central as overflow for non-PII traffic. Doing steps 1+2 now.

emma: running command to flip throttling:
```
redwoodctl routing update --hosted --throttle-global 0.85 --reason "incident 1842509876"
```

ops-bot: executed by emma at 02:18 UTC: throttling set to 85% global capacity.

siva: enabling model_fallback policy, hotfix patch applied to routing ruleset-119. Code snippet:
```
routing.ruleset-119.fallback = ["gpt-medium-quant", "gpt-small-quant"]
routing.ruleset-119.fallback_mode = "prefer-regional-compat"
```

ops-bot: routing.ruleset-119 updated by siva at 02:19 UTC.

emma: monitoring queue length and latencies. initial effect: queue growth rate slowed, p95 down to 2.1s, p99 to 9.6s, error rate still ~0.9% (was 2.6%). backlog at 02:25 -> 4.3k.

anya: looping in CS: @customer-success please prepare outbound. Which customers impacted and escalation level?

customer-success: preparing note. Impacted customers list (prelim): AcmeCorp (SLA: premium), Tutorly (PLG but heavy), DataSage (batch embeddings). We'll coordinate a status update.

mike: provider quota request is pending but not instant. We should also consider local mitigations: bump worker concurrency on existing GPUs to improve throughput for short-token requests. That can increase latency variance but reduce queue.

emma: agreed. doing a staged concurrency bump for low-priority routes.
```
redwoodctl pool update --pool gpu-hosted-west --concurrency-increase 1.25 --routes "low-priority"
```

ops-bot: command started by emma at 02:30 UTC.

pagerduty-bot: Incident assigned to emma (Oncall SRE) at 02:31 UTC. Severity: SEV2.

emma: quick customer impact summary for timeline:
- start: 02:10 UTC queue growth begins after sudden traffic spike from a partner campaign
- 02:12-02:20 UTC p99 up to 18s, errors/timeouts spike to 2.6%
- 02:18 UTC throttling enabled, fallback enabled
- 02:25 UTC partial stabilization, p99 ~9.6s, errors 0.9%
- 02:30 UTC concurrency bump started, backlog 4.3k -> trending down

anya: good. recommendation: declare incident and run for 90m with oncall rotation, CS to notify top-tier customers in 30m with mitigation note and ETA for full recovery.

emma: declaring incident and creating incident doc: https://incidents.redwood.ai/1842509876

siva: note — autoscaler operator logs show a recurring stacktrace referencing the cloud provider API returning 429 on quota check. We'll file a provider-issue and track separately. For now, fallback and throttling are primary mitigations.

mike: can we spin up a temporary dedicated pool (provider-side) using our reserved-capacity contracts in another region? Might be faster than quota increase. Ops, please estimate time.

emma: spinning up a dedicated small pool in eu-central for overflow (non-PII). If successful, will route low-reward requests there. ETA ~12-18m.

ops-bot: pool create job started by emma at 02:38 UTC. job_id=job-88f3.

emma: handoff plan — I'm primary for the next 35m, then handing to siva for the overnight window. Siva, please take over at 03:15 UTC if still ongoing.

siva: acknowledged, I'll take over at 03:15. I'll also follow up with provider account team for quota check and file provider ticket.

customer-success: sending first customer note at 02:42 UTC to affected accounts. Template attached and will include fallback and ETA.

mike: monitoring: queue down to 2.1k at 02:45 UTC, p95 1.8s, p99 6.4s, errors 0.4%. Good trend.

emma: eu-central pool is up at 02:50 UTC, routing tests pass. Starting slow drain of eligible traffic.

ops-bot: traffic overflow routing enabled by emma at 02:52 UTC for non-PII routes.

anya: CS update: customers acknowledged, one enterprise asked for timeline on full recovery and permanent SLA remediation plan. We'll coordinate a follow-up tomorrow.

emma: leaving the incident doc with timeline and mitigations. continuing monitoring. handoff reminder to siva at 03:15 UTC.

siva: took over at 03:15 UTC. will keep incident open until backlog < 500 and p99 < 500ms for 20m. current backlog 1.2k, p99 2.1s.

emma: thanks all. postmortem to include: autoscaler operator resilience to provider 429s, better preflight on quota, and routing priorities to avoid single region saturation.

ops-bot: incident 1842509876 updated: status=monitoring, severity=SEV2, owner=siva.
